feature: A new video keeps the length it was given
summary: A video made with File > New Video at ten seconds stays ten seconds when a shorter title page goes on it. Something longer still makes it longer, and taking that away goes back to ten, not to the title's four.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Checked with the walk new-video-keeps-its-length-walk on the probe, screen unlocked, Screen Recording granted.

try.do: File > New > Video, and press Return to take 1920 by 1080 at ten seconds.
In the Library, open Catalog, pick Main Title and click Insert at Playhead. The title bar still says 0:10 and the ruler still runs to 10s.
File > Import Media, then drag the recording from the Library onto the timeline four seconds in. The video grows to 0:12.
Click the recording on the timeline and press Delete. The video goes back to 0:10.
File > Export as an MP4. The file runs ten seconds: the title, then the six seconds after it.

evaluate: Is ten seconds still what you expect after the title goes on, rather than four?
After deleting the longer recording, is going back to ten (not four) what you wanted?
Should the six seconds after the title export as the title's last frame held, or would you rather they were black?
rough: Only a video started with New Video remembers a chosen length. A recording, a cut or an opened movie is still exactly as long as what is on it.
There is no way to change the chosen length after the video is made; the New Video sheet is the only place it is set.
In the walk the recording dragged at the empty V1 landed on a new V2 track instead, with the title's rows above it. Not this task; noted in its log.
